answer: Persistent Compute Ledger: each identity must continuously produce unique, verifiable work traces on dedicated physical hardware whose serial numbers and tamper logs are attested at the silicon level. A garden of idle identities fails because the ledger demands sustained, non-replayable computation tied to that exact device. Cross-checking against a shared reef of historical work signatures catches cloned traces. Every new identity must bridge its ledger to an existing verified one through a hardware-attested handshake,
